metadata.title: Product Streams
metadata.description: Outcome-based product streams for the Real Estate ERP Platform domain: the real estate lifecycle Portfolio -> Let -> Contract -> Collect -> Maintain -> Account -> Report -> Serve as run by investors, asset managers, property managers and VvE administrators on the combined Bloxs + Informant platform, plus the project, portal and automation journeys that hang off it.
metadata.flowModelNote: Each stream carries only stream-specific flows, names the supporting bricks used in each step and the persona acting in it, and lists the external systems (banks, e-signing, rent-price check, maintenance partners, e-invoicing, public registers, BI and e-mail platforms) the flow depends on.

rootGroups.name: Portfolio and Letting Journeys
rootGroups.description: From a legacy system, spreadsheet or acquisition to a live portfolio, and from a vacant unit to a lease that runs through indexation, changes, settlements and termination without errors: the journeys that put objects, relations and contracts at the heart of the platform.

streams.name: Onboard Portfolio and Entities
streams.description: Take a real estate organisation from contracts, spreadsheets or a legacy system such as Informant to a complete, reconciled portfolio in the ERP: legal entities and owner mandates, objects, complexes and units, relations, running contracts with their components and deposits, and opening balances that match the old books to the cent.
outcomes: Every migrated or acquired portfolio invoices correctly in its first rent run, because contracts, components and mandates were validated before go-live
Trial balances per entity match the legacy closing balance, so the first period close on the platform is auditable
Informant customers migrate in phased waves without losing service, and acquired portfolios are live by the transfer date

flows.title: Migrate an Informant Portfolio to the Platform
flows.description: The phased, free-of-charge migration of a property manager or VvE administrator from Informant: extract, map, validate, reconcile opening balances, rehearse and cut over without losing trusted service.
flows.trigger: An Informant customer signs the migration agreement and the customer-success team schedules the migration wave.
flows.successSignal: The customer runs its first rent run and owner statements on the new platform, the trial balance per entity matches the Informant closing balance to the cent and Informant is set to read-only.

steps.title: Extract and profile the Informant database
keyFacts: A typical Informant customer holds several hundred to a few thousand units across dozens of owner mandates and associations, with contracts, contacts, ledgers and documents accumulated over up to 25 years.

The migration tooling profiles the extract first: duplicate contacts, units without a valid address, contracts without an end or indexation clause and unbalanced ledgers are listed before any mapping starts.
painPoints: Legacy free-text fields (rent components typed into notes, IBANs in remarks) are invisible until someone reads every record.
Without a profile the customer discovers data quality problems in the first rent run instead of in the workshop.

dependencies.name: Data Migration and Onboarding Tooling
dependencies.description: Extraction profiles and data quality report per source system.
dependencies.how: Loads the Informant extract into a staging area and produces the quality report that drives the mapping workshop.

dependencies.name: Informant Legacy System
dependencies.description: The acquired Informant property management and VvE administration system from which customers are migrated free of charge, with Informant support until 31 December 2027.
dependencies.interface: Database extracts and migration files
dependencies.how: Supplies the database extract, document store and open-item lists for the migration wave.

steps.title: Map entities, mandates and portfolio structures
keyFacts: Every owner mandate, investment entity (BV, CV, fund) and association becomes its own administration with its own ledger, bank accounts and access rights, while the manager keeps one cross-entity view.
The object hierarchy is rebuilt as portfolio, complex, building and unit with BAG identifiers, so an Informant 'object' with five apartments becomes one complex with five rentable units.
painPoints: Legacy systems mixed owner money and management-fee money in one ledger, which the new multi-entity model must untangle before go-live.
Unit numbering conventions differ per manager, and a wrong split breaks every downstream report.

dependencies.name: Data Migration and Onboarding Tooling
dependencies.description: Mapping tables from legacy structures to the target model.
dependencies.how: Applies the agreed mapping of entities, mandates and object hierarchy and flags unmapped records.

dependencies.name: Objects, Complexes and Units
dependencies.description: Target object, complex and unit model.
dependencies.how: Creates the portfolio hierarchy with addresses, surfaces and unit types.

dependencies.name: Identity, Tenants and Access

dependencies.how: Creates the organisation, its administrations and the role assignments per entity.

dependencies.name: Kadaster and BAG Registers

dependencies.interface: BAG address and building lookup, Kadaster ownership and parcel extracts
dependencies.how: Validates addresses and building identifiers against the BAG during mapping.

steps.title: Cleanse and deduplicate relations
keyFacts: Tenants, owners, suppliers and accountants are merged into one relation record each, with KvK number, IBAN, roles per entity and communication preferences.
The same person may be a tenant of one owner and a board member of an association; roles are attached to the single relation instead of duplicated contacts.
painPoints: Duplicate contacts create double invoices and double reminders on day one.
IBANs that belong to a former tenant are silently reused when contacts are not cleansed.

dependencies.description: Single relation database with roles and identifiers.
dependencies.how: Receives the deduplicated relations with their roles per administration.

dependencies.name: Data Migration and Onboarding Tooling
dependencies.description: Match and merge rules for relations.
dependencies.how: Suggests merges on name, address, IBAN and KvK number for manual confirmation.

dependencies.name: KvK Business Register

dependencies.interface: KvK number lookup and company data API
dependencies.how: Validates KvK numbers and legal names of business relations.

steps.title: Load contracts, rent components and deposits
keyFacts: Each lease is loaded with its start date, notice terms, rent components (basic rent, service charge advances, VAT status), indexation clause and deposit held, so the first indexation and settlement can run from history.
Contracts under the Dutch 290 retail regime, 230a office regime and residential regime carry different rules; the contract type is set explicitly at load.
painPoints: Indexation history missing from the legacy export means the next indexation cannot be justified to the tenant.
Deposits recorded as free text cannot be settled at termination.

dependencies.name: Documents and Correspondence

steps.title: Reconcile opening balances per entity
keyFacts: Open debtor items, deposits held, supplier liabilities, association reserve funds and bank balances are loaded per administration and reconciled to the Informant trial balance at the cut-over date.
Opening balances are booked to a migration date so the first period on the new platform starts clean and auditable.
painPoints: A trial balance that does not match by a few euros costs days of searching at year end.
Deposits held for tenants are the most common item to go missing between systems.

steps.title: Rehearse the first rent run and sign off
keyFacts: A rehearsal rent run and owner statement are produced on the migrated data and compared line by line with the last Informant run before the customer signs off.
Users train on their own data during the rehearsal, which is when most mapping questions surface.
painPoints: Migrations signed off on record counts alone produce a wrong first invoice to every tenant.
Training on demo data leaves users lost on go-live day.

dependencies.how: Produces owner statements from the migrated data for comparison with the legacy statements.

steps.title: Cut over, invite portal users and set Informant read-only
keyFacts: Cut-over freezes the legacy system, loads the final delta, activates direct debit mandates and invites tenants, owners and suppliers to the portals.
Informant remains available read-only, with support running until 31 December 2027, so historic questions can still be answered.
painPoints: A cut-over without a delta load loses the last days of payments and tickets.
Portal invitations sent before data is trusted generate a wave of support calls.

dependencies.interface: Transactional e-mail, app push and SMS
dependencies.how: Sends portal invitations and the go-live announcement.

flows.title: Onboard a Newly Acquired Portfolio
flows.description: An investor or manager takes over a portfolio from a seller or another manager: set up entities, register objects and units, load contracts from the data room and start invoicing from the transfer date.
flows.trigger: A share or asset deal closes and the transfer date for a portfolio of, for example, 120 residential units and 8 commercial units is fixed.
flows.successSignal: All units, contracts and tenants are live with correct rent components by the transfer date and the first rent run invoices from day one of ownership.

steps.title: Set up the acquiring entities and bank accounts
keyFacts: Each acquiring vehicle gets its own administration with chart of accounts, VAT regime, bank accounts and reporting currency; German entities get the German chart and VAT settings.
Management fee agreements between the manager and the entity are configured once so the fee is invoiced automatically.
painPoints: Entities created ad hoc without a template drift in chart of accounts, making consolidation manual.
Missing bank account links delay the first reconciliation by weeks.

dependencies.description: Administration templates and chart of accounts.
dependencies.how: Creates the entity ledger from the group template.

dependencies.name: Identity, Tenants and Access
dependencies.how: Grants the asset manager, controller and property manager access to the new administration.

dependencies.name: Bank Integration and Reconciliation
dependencies.how: Registers the entity's IBANs for statement retrieval and direct debit.

steps.title: Register objects and units from the data room
keyFacts: Units are created with address, BAG identifier, surface (NEN 2580), unit type, energy label and WWS points where applicable, so letting and rent-price checks work from the start.
Parcels and ownership are verified against the Kadaster extract to make sure every unit in the deal is actually transferred.
painPoints: Units typed from the seller's rent roll inherit the seller's errors.
Missing energy labels block new lettings because the label must be handed over at signing.

dependencies.name: Objects, Complexes and Units
dependencies.description: Object and unit registration with identifiers.
dependencies.how: Creates complexes and units with their attributes and identifiers.

dependencies.name: Data Migration and Onboarding Tooling
dependencies.how: Imports the seller's rent roll into objects, units and contracts with validation.

dependencies.interface: BAG address and building lookup, Kadaster ownership and parcel extracts
dependencies.how: Verifies parcels, addresses and ownership of the acquired objects.

steps.title: Load tenants and running contracts
keyFacts: Running leases transfer to the buyer by law ('koop breekt geen huur'); every contract is loaded with its rent components, indexation clause, deposit and service charge advances.
Tenants are informed of the new landlord and the new payment details, and existing direct debit mandates are migrated or re-issued.
painPoints: Deposits not transferred by the seller surface only when the first tenant leaves.
Tenants paying the old landlord for months after transfer create reconciliation chaos.

dependencies.name: Lease Contracts and E-Signing
dependencies.description: Contract loading with clauses and deposits.
dependencies.how: Creates the leases and their components for the acquired units.

dependencies.name: Relations and CRM
dependencies.how: Creates or matches the tenant relations with their contact details.

dependencies.name: Documents and Correspondence
dependencies.how: Generates and files the change-of-landlord letter per tenant.

steps.title: Load valuations, capex plan and asset plan
keyFacts: The acquisition valuation, the technical due diligence findings and the initial capex plan become the baseline for the asset plan and the multi-year maintenance budget.
Installations found in the due diligence (boilers, lifts, fire systems) are registered so inspections are scheduled from day one.
painPoints: Due diligence reports left in the data room are never turned into planned work.
Without a valuation baseline the first investor report cannot show value creation.

dependencies.name: Valuations and Market Data
dependencies.how: Stores the acquisition value and valuer report as the first valuation record.

dependencies.name: Multi-Year Maintenance Planning and Budgets
dependencies.how: Creates the capex and maintenance plan from due diligence findings.

dependencies.name: Installations and Periodic Maintenance
dependencies.how: Registers installations and their inspection regimes for the acquired objects.

steps.title: Start invoicing from the transfer date
keyFacts: Rent for the transfer month is split between seller and buyer pro rata; the platform invoices the buyer's share and books the seller settlement.
Service charge advances continue while the settlement for the seller's part of the year is agreed in the completion statement.
painPoints: Pro rata splits done in a spreadsheet are argued over for months in the completion accounts.
A first rent run with wrong bank details teaches tenants to ignore the new landlord.

dependencies.name: Rent Invoicing and Billing Runs
dependencies.description: Pro rata invoicing from the transfer date.
dependencies.how: Generates the first billing run with pro rata amounts.

dependencies.name: Service Charges and Settlements
dependencies.description: Service charge advances and settlement periods.
dependencies.how: Continues advances and opens the settlement period from the transfer date.

dependencies.name: Multi-Entity General Ledger and Period Close
dependencies.how: Books the seller-buyer settlement in the entity ledger.

steps.title: Hand over to property management and open the portals
keyFacts: The property manager receives the objects, contracts and open tickets in one view and tenants get portal access to pay, report faults and read their contract.
Owner and investor reporting starts with the first monthly close after transfer.
painPoints: Hand-over by e-mail loses the open maintenance issues the seller did not fix.
Tenants who cannot find their new landlord online call and complain instead of paying.

dependencies.name: Workflow, Tasks and Notifications
dependencies.how: Creates the hand-over checklist and assigns open items to the property manager.

dependencies.name: Tenant Portal and App
dependencies.how: Invites tenants of the acquired units to the portal and app.

dependencies.name: Investor and Owner Reporting
dependencies.how: Includes the acquired portfolio in the next reporting period.

streams.name: Let Units and Sign Contracts
streams.description: Take a property manager or asset manager from a vacant unit to a signed, invoicing lease: listing and viewings, candidate screening within the Good Landlord Act, rent-price check on the WWS points, contract generation from templates, electronic signing, deposit and first rent, key hand-over with an inspection report, and commercial lettings with brokers, incentives and special terms.
outcomes: Fewer vacancy days per turnover, because listing, viewings, screening, signing and payment run in one flow instead of across e-mail, Word and the bank
Every new letting is rent-price compliant and documented, so Rent Tribunal reductions and Good Landlord Act fines are avoided
Contracts are captured once as structured data, so indexation, settlements, break options and terminations run from the contract without re-keying

flows.title: Let a Vacant Dwelling Compliantly
flows.description: From notice of termination to a signed residential lease: publish the vacancy, run viewings, screen candidates within the Good Landlord Act, check the rent price against the WWS points, generate and e-sign the contract, collect deposit and first rent and hand over the keys.
flows.trigger: A tenant gives notice on a three-room apartment and the unit becomes available in one month.
flows.successSignal: A new tenant has signed electronically, paid deposit and first rent, received the keys with an inspection report and the contract is invoicing from the start date.

steps.title: Register the vacancy and set the asking rent
keyFacts: The unit's WWS points decide whether the dwelling is regulated, mid-rent or free sector; since the Affordable Rent Act of 1 July 2024 the mid-rent segment is capped by points as well, so the asking rent is checked before publication.
Market rent references from comparable lettings in the portfolio and external data support the asking rent for free-sector units.
painPoints: An asking rent above the legal maximum can be reduced by the Rent Tribunal and fined by the municipality under the Good Landlord Act.
Vacancy days start counting from the notice date, not from the first viewing.

dependencies.name: Vacancy, Letting and Candidate Screening
dependencies.description: Vacancy record with asking rent and publication.
dependencies.how: Creates the vacancy and its asking rent, publication texts and photos.

dependencies.name: Objects, Complexes and Units
dependencies.description: Unit attributes, surface, energy label and WWS points.
dependencies.how: Provides the unit data that determine the rent regime.

dependencies.name: Huurprijscheck.app Rent-Price Check
dependencies.description: Calculates the housing valuation system (WWS) points and the maximum legal rent of a dwelling so a letting is checked for rent-price compliance before the contract is issued.
dependencies.interface: WWS points calculation and maximum-rent API
dependencies.how: Calculates the WWS points and the maximum legal rent for the unit before publication.

steps.title: Publish the listing and plan viewings
keyFacts: The listing is published to the organisation's own website and partner portals with a transparent selection procedure, as the Good Landlord Act requires.
Viewing slots are booked online and confirmed by e-mail, with candidate interest captured in the vacancy record.
painPoints: Viewings planned by phone consume the property manager's afternoons.
Interest tracked in an inbox makes the selection procedure impossible to document.

dependencies.name: Vacancy, Letting and Candidate Screening
dependencies.how: Publishes the listing and manages viewing slots and interest.

dependencies.name: Workflow, Tasks and Notifications
dependencies.how: Sends viewing confirmations and reminders to candidates.

dependencies.name: E-mail, Push and SMS Gateway
dependencies.description: Delivers rent invoices, pre-notifications, reminders, ticket updates, meeting convocations and portal invitations to tenants, owners and suppliers.
dependencies.interface: Transactional e-mail, app push and SMS
dependencies.how: Delivers viewing confirmations and reminders by e-mail and SMS.

steps.title: Screen candidates and document the selection
keyFacts: Candidates upload identity, income and employer documents in a portal; income norms (for example gross income of three to four times the rent) and credit checks are applied consistently, and the choice is documented with objective criteria.
Only data necessary for the decision is stored, and rejected candidates' documents are deleted after the retention period, as the GDPR and the Good Landlord Act demand.
painPoints: Copies of passports in mailboxes are a data breach waiting to happen.
Undocumented selection exposes the manager to discrimination complaints.

dependencies.name: Vacancy, Letting and Candidate Screening
dependencies.how: Captures applications, runs the screening rules and records the selection rationale.

dependencies.name: Relations and CRM
dependencies.how: Creates the candidate as a relation with restricted retention.

dependencies.name: Credit and Identity Check Providers
dependencies.description: Screening providers used during candidate selection to verify identity, income and payment history within the rules of the Good Landlord Act and GDPR.
dependencies.interface: Credit score, identity verification and income check APIs
dependencies.how: Verifies identity, income and payment history of the selected candidates.

steps.title: Generate the lease from the contract template
keyFacts: The contract is generated from the template for the rent regime (regulated, mid-rent, free sector) with rent components, service charge advances, deposit of at most two months' basic rent and the mandatory information for tenants.
Temporary contracts are only allowed in the exceptions that survived the Fixed Rental Contracts Act of 1 July 2024; the template enforces the contract type.
painPoints: Contracts edited in Word drift from the model and miss mandatory clauses.
A deposit above two months' rent is unlawful and must be refunded.

dependencies.name: Lease Contracts and E-Signing
dependencies.how: Creates the lease with components, deposit and clauses from the chosen template.

dependencies.name: Documents and Correspondence
dependencies.how: Compiles the lease PDF with energy label, house rules and information sheet.

dependencies.name: AI Assistants
dependencies.how: Suggests wording for special terms within the template rules.

steps.title: E-sign the contract and collect deposit and first rent
keyFacts: The tenant signs in the e-signing flow and pays deposit and first rent through a payment link or bank transfer; a SEPA direct debit mandate is signed in the same session.
The signed contract with audit trail is filed on the relation and the unit, and the contract is activated on receipt of payment.
painPoints: Paper contracts sent by post add a week to the vacancy.
Keys handed over before the deposit is received are the start of every bad tenancy.

dependencies.name: Lease Contracts and E-Signing
dependencies.how: Sends the contract for signature and activates it once signed and paid.

dependencies.name: Bank Integration and Reconciliation
dependencies.how: Matches the incoming payment to the contract and registers the SEPA mandate.

steps.title: Hand over keys with an inspection report
keyFacts: The check-in inspection records the condition per room with photos and meter readings; it is signed by both parties in the app and becomes the reference for the check-out.
Meter readings are passed to the tenant for their energy contracts and to service charge settlement where applicable.
painPoints: Without a signed check-in report the landlord cannot deduct damage from the deposit.
Meter readings on paper are lost by the time the settlement is made.

dependencies.how: Stores the signed check-in report with photos and readings.

dependencies.name: Objects, Complexes and Units
dependencies.how: Records meter readings and condition at the start of the tenancy.

dependencies.name: Tenant Portal and App
dependencies.how: Lets the tenant view and sign the report in the app.

steps.title: Activate invoicing and the tenant portal
keyFacts: The active contract enters the next rent run with pro rata rent for the first month; the direct debit mandate is pre-notified and the tenant sees invoices and documents in the portal.
Vacancy days and time-to-let are closed on the vacancy record for the property manager's KPI.
painPoints: Contracts activated after the rent run miss a month of collection.
Tenants without portal access call the office for every question.

dependencies.name: Rent Invoicing and Billing Runs
dependencies.how: Schedules the pro rata first invoice and the recurring rent.

dependencies.name: Tenant Portal and App
dependencies.how: Invites the tenant and shows contract, invoices and documents.

dependencies.name: Vacancy, Letting and Candidate Screening
dependencies.how: Closes the vacancy and records vacancy days and time-to-let.

flows.title: Let Commercial Space and Negotiate the Lease
flows.description: From an empty office or retail unit to a signed ROZ-model lease: marketing through brokers, proposals with incentives, credit assessment of the business tenant, negotiated special terms, e-signing and fit-out hand-over.
flows.trigger: A 1,200 m2 office floor becomes vacant after a break option is exercised.
flows.successSignal: A creditworthy business tenant has signed a multi-year lease with agreed incentives, and rent, service charges and VAT are invoicing from the commencement date.

steps.title: Brief brokers and publish the availability
keyFacts: Commercial vacancies are marketed through brokers under a mandate with agreed fees; the availability sheet carries surface per NEN 2580, asking rent per m2, service charge estimate and delivery level.
Broker leads and viewings are logged on the vacancy so the asset manager sees the pipeline per unit.
painPoints: Availability lists maintained by brokers show units already let.
Leads kept by brokers are lost when the mandate ends.

dependencies.name: Vacancy, Letting and Candidate Screening
dependencies.description: Commercial vacancy with broker mandate and leads.
dependencies.how: Registers the vacancy, mandate, lead pipeline and viewings.

dependencies.name: Relations and CRM
dependencies.how: Holds broker and prospect relations and their contacts.

steps.title: Issue a proposal with rent, incentives and term
keyFacts: A proposal defines rent, indexation clause, term (for example 5+5 years under the retail regime), rent-free months, fit-out contribution and break options, with the effective rent calculated over the term.
Proposal versions are kept so the asset manager can compare negotiated variants and their effect on the cash flow.
painPoints: Effective rent calculated in a spreadsheet differs from what finance books later.
Incentives agreed by e-mail never reach the invoicing schedule.

dependencies.name: Lease Contracts and E-Signing
dependencies.how: Creates the proposal with incentives and term as a draft contract.

dependencies.name: Dashboards and Data Analytics
dependencies.description: Effective rent and cash flow effect.
dependencies.how: Calculates the effective rent and shows the cash flow impact per variant.

steps.title: Assess tenant credit and security
keyFacts: The business tenant is checked on KvK data, financial statements and credit score; security is set as a deposit or bank guarantee, typically three months' rent plus service charges and VAT.
Guarantees are registered with expiry dates so they can be called or renewed before they lapse.
painPoints: Bank guarantees in a drawer expire unnoticed.
A tenant that fails within a year costs more than the vacancy it filled.

dependencies.name: Vacancy, Letting and Candidate Screening
dependencies.how: Records the assessment and the required security.

dependencies.name: Relations and CRM

dependencies.how: Stores the legal entity, signatories and group structure.

dependencies.description: Chamber of Commerce register used to validate business tenants, suppliers and legal entities and to register owners' associations.
dependencies.interface: KvK number lookup and company data API
dependencies.how: Provides the registered company data and signatories.

dependencies.description: Screening providers used during candidate selection to verify identity, income and payment history within the rules of the Good Landlord Act and GDPR.
dependencies.interface: Credit score, identity verification and income check APIs
dependencies.how: Supplies the credit score of the business tenant.

steps.title: Negotiate special terms and VAT option
keyFacts: Special terms (exclusivity, expansion rights, indexation floors, sustainability obligations) are recorded as structured clauses; the VAT-taxed lease option is only valid when the tenant uses the space for at least 90 percent VAT-taxed activities.
Break options and renewal notice dates become dated obligations that trigger tasks years later.
painPoints: Special terms buried in the PDF are forgotten by the time they matter.
An invalid VAT option leads to VAT corrections on the landlord's investment costs.

dependencies.name: Lease Contracts and E-Signing
dependencies.description: Structured special clauses and VAT option.

dependencies.name: VAT and Tax Handling
dependencies.how: Sets the taxed or exempt treatment for invoicing and pro rata deduction.

dependencies.name: Workflow, Tasks and Notifications
dependencies.how: Creates tasks for break, renewal and obligation dates.

steps.title: Sign electronically with the authorised signatories
keyFacts: The ROZ-model lease and general conditions are signed by the authorised signatories of both entities in a multi-party e-signing flow with identity verification.
The signed contract is filed on the entity, unit and tenant relation with the guarantee document.
painPoints: Wet-ink signatures with couriers add weeks to commencement.
Signatures by unauthorised persons make the lease contestable.

dependencies.name: Lease Contracts and E-Signing

dependencies.name: Documents and Correspondence

dependencies.how: Provides multi-signer envelopes with identity verification.

steps.title: Deliver the space and start invoicing
keyFacts: Delivery is recorded with a signed report and photos; rent-free months are applied as scheduled credits so invoices show the agreed rent from the commencement date.
Service charge advances and VAT are invoiced with the rent, and the fit-out contribution is paid against the tenant's invoice.
painPoints: Rent-free periods applied by hand in the rent run are the most common invoicing error on commercial leases.
Delivery disputes without a signed report end up in court.

streams.name: Manage Leases Through Their Lifecycle
streams.description: Take every signed lease through its life without errors: annual rent indexation with the legal caps per segment and jurisdiction, special terms and break options as dated obligations, changes and renewals, terminations with deposit settlement within the legal term, and annual service charge settlements issued on time.
outcomes: The indexation round is completed in days with every increase within the legal cap and every letter sent in time
Deposits are settled within 14 days and service charge statements within the legal term, so tribunal cases and forfeited claims disappear
Break options, renewals and obligations surface as tasks years ahead, so no rent growth or notice date is missed

flows.title: Run the Annual Rent Indexation
flows.description: The yearly indexation round across residential and commercial contracts: determine the applicable index and legal cap per contract, calculate proposals, review exceptions, generate and send the rent increase letters in time and update the rent components for the next run.
flows.trigger: The government publishes the maximum residential rent increase for the coming year and the CBS publishes the consumer price index the commercial contracts refer to.
flows.successSignal: Every eligible contract has a correct new rent effective on its indexation date, tenants were notified within the legal notice period, and the next rent run invoices the new amounts.

steps.title: Determine the index and legal cap per contract
keyFacts: Residential increases are capped per segment and year (in the Netherlands the free-sector cap follows the lower of inflation or wage growth plus one percentage point; regulated and mid-rent segments have their own caps), while commercial ROZ contracts follow the CPI clause in the lease.
German contracts distinguish index rent (Indexmiete), stepped rent (Staffelmiete) and increases to the local comparative rent with the capping limit of 15 or 20 percent over three years.
painPoints: Applying one percentage to all contracts is the classic error that triggers Rent Tribunal cases.
Contracts with custom index clauses (floors, caps, different base months) are skipped or wrongly indexed.

dependencies.name: Lease Contracts and E-Signing

steps.title: Calculate proposals and review the exceptions
keyFacts: The round calculates the new rent per contract and flags exceptions: rent above the WWS maximum, income-dependent increases, contracts within a rent-free period, tenants with an open Rent Tribunal case.
Property managers review a worklist of exceptions instead of every contract; the rest is approved in bulk.
painPoints: Reviewing thousands of contracts by hand takes weeks every spring.
Increases above the point-based maximum are unenforceable and must be reversed.

Approvals are logged with the decision and become part of the owner statement narrative.
painPoints: Approvals by e-mail cannot be found when the tenant disputes the increase.
Owners who are not asked feel bypassed and leave the manager.

Commercial index letters state the index figures and the calculation so the tenant can verify the new rent.

Mail-merged letters with wrong figures cannot be recalled.

flows.title: Terminate a Lease and Settle Deposit and Service Charges
flows.description: From a tenant's notice to a settled tenancy: validate the notice period, plan the check-out inspection, settle damage and the deposit within the legal term, make the final invoice and service charge settlement, and release the unit to letting.
flows.trigger: A tenant sends notice through the tenant portal that they will leave at the end of next month.
flows.successSignal: The deposit is returned within 14 days after the tenancy ends, the final invoice and settlement are booked, and the unit is in the letting pipeline without a gap.

steps.title: Register the notice and validate the notice period
keyFacts: A residential tenant's notice period equals the payment term (one month); a landlord's notice is three to six months and only on statutory grounds. Commercial notice terms follow the lease and regime.
The end date is confirmed to the tenant in writing and the unit is pre-registered as upcoming vacancy.
painPoints: Notices received by phone are disputed later.
A wrong end date shifts the whole letting timeline.

steps.title: Plan the pre-inspection and check-out
keyFacts: A pre-inspection gives the tenant a list of items to restore before the check-out; the check-out compares the unit with the check-in report and records meter readings and returned keys.
Both inspections are signed in the app and produce the evidence for any deduction.
painPoints: Without a pre-inspection every check-out ends in an argument about who pays for what.
Missing meter readings leave the energy supplier to guess the final bill.

steps.title: Order restoration work if needed
keyFacts: Damage beyond normal wear is priced by a supplier quote and, where the mandate allows, charged to the departing tenant.
Restoration and mutation maintenance are planned so that the unit is ready before the next tenant's start date.
painPoints: Restoration ordered after the check-out extends the vacancy by weeks.
Unpriced damage cannot be deducted from the deposit.

steps.title: Settle the deposit within the legal term
keyFacts: Under the Good Landlord Act the deposit is returned within 14 days after the end of the lease, or within 30 days with an itemised statement when costs are deducted.
The settlement nets deposit, open rent, damage and keys against each other and pays the balance by SEPA credit transfer.
painPoints: Deposits paid late generate complaints to the municipality and negative reviews.
Manual netting of open items produces wrong payouts.

keyFacts: The last rent is pro-rated to the end date; service charges are settled for the tenant's part of the year against actual costs, and the residential settlement overview is due within six months after the calendar year.
Interim settlements are estimated from the current year's budget and finalised in the annual round.
painPoints: Tenants who left are hard to reach for a settlement a year later.
Forgotten interim settlements leave money on both sides.

The tenancy is archived with its documents for the legal retention period.

Archived tenancies without documents cannot answer later claims.

flows.title: Settle Annual Service Charges
flows.description: The annual settlement round for a complex: collect actual costs, allocate them per unit with the agreed keys, compare with advances, issue statements to tenants within the legal term and adjust the advances for the coming year.
flows.trigger: The financial year closes and all supplier invoices for the complex's service costs (cleaning, energy of common areas, lift, caretaker) are booked.
flows.successSignal: Every tenant received a correct settlement statement within the legal term, differences are invoiced or refunded, and next year's advances are updated.

steps.title: Collect the actual service costs per complex
keyFacts: Service costs are booked on cost categories per complex during the year; only costs that are chargeable under the lease and the law (for residential the Service Costs Decree) may be settled.
Commercial leases may include an administration fee of, for example, five percent on top of the costs.
painPoints: Costs booked to the wrong complex are only found when tenants complain.
Non-chargeable costs in the settlement are reversed by the Rent Tribunal.

steps.title: Allocate costs with keys and compare to advances
keyFacts: Costs are allocated per unit by surface, share, number of units or metered consumption, pro rata for tenants who moved in or out during the year, and compared with the advances invoiced.
The allocation keys are stored on the contract and complex, so the settlement is reproducible year after year.
painPoints: Spreadsheet allocations break when one tenant moved mid-year.
Keys that differ between the lease and the spreadsheet cause disputes.

keyFacts: The property manager reviews outliers (large differences, negative settlements, tenants without advances) and the owner approves the settlement for managed portfolios.
Approved settlements are locked and become the basis for statements and bookings.
painPoints: Settlements sent without review produce refunds that are then reclaimed.
Owners surprised by refunds question the manager's competence.

steps.title: Issue statements and book the differences
keyFacts: Each tenant receives a statement with the cost categories, their share, the advances paid and the difference; residential statements must be issued within six months after the year, German operating cost statements within twelve months.
Differences are invoiced or credited in the next rent run and booked to the entity ledger.
painPoints: A statement issued after the legal term forfeits the landlord's claim for additional payment.
Differences booked manually are missed in the debtor administration.

Advance changes not passed to the rent run make next year's settlement wrong again.

rootGroups.name: Rent, Finance and Steering Journeys
rootGroups.description: From active contracts to money in the bank, from transactions to closed entities and investor packs, and from portfolio data to hold, invest or sell decisions: the journeys that make the platform a real estate accounting and steering system rather than a card index.

streams.name: Invoice and Collect Rent
streams.description: Take every active contract to money in the bank each period: validated billing runs per entity, invoices by portal, e-mail and Peppol, SEPA direct debit with correct pre-notification, daily CAMT.053 reconciliation with automatic matching, R-transaction handling, and dunning paths with payment plans, early signalling and bailiff hand-over.
outcomes: Rent collection rate above 98 percent within the month, with the direct debit batch executed on the due date for every entity
More than 95 percent of bank statement lines matched automatically, so finance works a short worklist instead of a spreadsheet
Arrears below two percent with every overdue tenant on a compliant reminder path, payment plan or early-signalling report

flows.title: Run the Monthly Rent Run with SEPA Direct Debit
flows.description: The periodic billing cycle for all entities: generate rent invoices from active contracts, pre-notify direct debit tenants, submit the SEPA batch, collect the CAMT.053 statements and match every receipt automatically.
flows.trigger: The billing calendar reaches the invoice date for next month's rent, typically around the 20th, across all administrations.
flows.successSignal: All invoices are sent, the direct debit batch is executed on the due date, and more than 95 percent of receipts are matched automatically on the next bank statement.

steps.title: Prepare and validate the billing run
keyFacts: The run selects every active contract per entity and builds invoice lines from the rent components: basic rent, service charge advances, VAT where applicable, indexation effective this period and one-off items such as settlement differences.
Validation flags contracts without a debtor, units with two active contracts, negative amounts and mandates that expired, before anything is invoiced.
painPoints: A run started without validation sends hundreds of wrong invoices that must be credited one by one.
Contract changes made after the run are invoiced a month late.

steps.title: Generate and send the invoices
keyFacts: Invoices are generated per entity with the entity's own layout, numbering and bank account; private tenants receive them by portal and e-mail, business tenants optionally as UBL e-invoices.
Owners and business tenants that demand e-invoicing are served via Peppol, which is increasingly required by larger organisations.
painPoints: Invoices from the wrong entity or with the wrong IBAN are paid to the wrong account and must be transferred manually.
PDF invoices e-mailed from a mailbox are not traceable when a tenant claims to have received nothing.

Mandate references, sequence types (first, recurring) and creditor identifiers are managed per entity so the bank accepts the batch.

flows.title: Follow Up Arrears with Dunning and Payment Plans
flows.description: From an unpaid invoice to money received or a controlled escalation: automated reminder paths per debtor type, the mandatory 14-day letter, payment plans, early signalling to the municipality for residential tenants and hand-over to the bailiff.
flows.trigger: The nightly arrears check finds invoices unpaid more than seven days after the due date.
flows.successSignal: Arrears are below two percent of monthly rent, every overdue tenant is on a reminder path or payment plan, and residential arrears older than the threshold have been reported for early signalling.

keyFacts: Reminder paths differ for private tenants (friendly reminder, formal reminder, the statutory 14-day letter before collection costs), business tenants (statutory interest and the fixed 40 euro compensation) and owners in associations.
Tenants with a running payment plan, a dispute or a tribunal case are excluded from the automatic path.
painPoints: One reminder path for everyone breaches consumer protection rules and annoys good payers.
Reminders sent during a dispute escalate it.

Every reminder is filed on the debtor with delivery evidence.
painPoints: Reminders typed by hand go out late and inconsistently.
Collection costs charged without a correct 14-day letter are not recoverable.

outcomes: Ticket resolution time within target per urgency, with first-time-fix above 80 percent because suppliers arrive with photos, history and access details

Supplier invoices matched to orders and paid on term without manual work, and supplier performance measured per installation type

rootGroups.name: Portal, Project and Platform Journeys

Suppliers accept, plan, complete and invoice through the portal, with payment status visible and no phone calls

Projects are capitalised per unit at delivery and units are pre-let, so the building earns from day one
Warranties, installations and defects are handed to maintenance without a gap, and the project is formally closed

streams.name: Automate and Integrate the Back Office
streams.description: Take controllers, property managers and directors from repetitive tasks and disconnected systems to robots, AI assistants, certified integrations and API connections: process selection by hours saved, rule and threshold configuration, shadow mode, supervised execution with audit logs, and connections to accounting packages, banks, BI, e-mail and maintenance partners with scoped credentials and monitoring.
outcomes: Repetitive financial processes run unattended with humans handling exceptions, with hours saved measured per robot and entity
Every external system is connected through a certified integration or the open API with scoped credentials, not through exports
Integrations and robots survive releases and acquisitions because they run on versioned APIs and platform data, not screens

flows.title: Put a Robot on a Repetitive Financial Process
flows.description: From hours spent on a repetitive task to an unattended robot with human supervision: identify the process, configure the robot's rules and thresholds, run it in shadow mode, go live with exception handling and monitor its results.
flows.trigger: The controller spends two days a month coding supplier invoices and matching bank lines across 40 entities.
flows.successSignal: The robot processes the routine cases unattended, humans handle only the exceptions, and the hours saved are visible in the automation dashboard.

steps.title: Identify the process and its rules
keyFacts: Candidate processes are those with high volume and stable rules: invoice coding, bank matching, indexation letters, reminders, owner statements; the automation dashboard ranks them by hours per month.
The rules are written as conditions on the platform's own data (supplier, amount, object, history), not as screen scripts.
painPoints: Automating an unclear process automates the mess.
Screen-scraping robots break at every release.

steps.title: Configure confidence thresholds and approvals
keyFacts: Each robot decision carries a confidence; above the threshold it is executed, below it goes to a human worklist, and financial actions above an amount always need approval.
Thresholds are set per entity and can be tightened for new suppliers or tenants.
painPoints: A robot without thresholds pays a wrong invoice at full speed.
Approvals for every action defeat the purpose.
